title: Follow the debug events
description:
A debugger keeps a picture of its debuggee from the stream of debug events. Write `Tracker`, which processes simplified events and answers questions.

Each `Event` has a `kind` and, depending on the kind, a `base` address, a `name`, a `code` and a `firstChance` flag:

| kind | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `"load"` | A module `name` loaded at `base` |
| `"unload"` | The module at `base` unloaded |
| `"exception"` | An exception `code` at address `base`, first or second chance |
| `"exit"` | The process exited with `code` |

`handle(event)` returns what the debugger should tell Windows, as the lesson describes: `"continue"` for everything except exceptions that are not breakpoints (`0x80000003`), for which it returns `"not-handled"`.

The tracker also answers:

- `modules()`: the names of the currently loaded modules, ordered by base address;
- `crashed()`: whether a **second-chance** exception was seen;
- `exitCode()`: the exit code, or `std::nullopt` if the process has not exited.
hints: A `std::map` from base address to name keeps the modules sorted by address and makes unloading by address a single `erase`.
For exceptions: a second-chance one marks a crash; anything other than the breakpoint code is passed back as `"not-handled"`.
lessonTitle: A Minimal Debugger of Your Own
